text:
maria: Heads up — hitting repeated tail-latency spikes from warmup jobs in us-west1-warmup pool. Graphs point at shelf-03 PCIe/NVLink contention. https://grafana.redwood/incidents/1234 :confused:
ajay: I saw the alert, digging. GPU-side dma/pcie counters are spiking around the same times. Warmup batch jobs start in waves and seem to coincide with the shelf noise window.
sam: Are these warmup tasks coming from multi-tenant prefill or from a single noisy onboarding job?
maria: Mostly prefill + a few onboarding bursts tonight. Tenant ids in the traces: t-145, t-202, t-331 (mixed).
linh: That mix is bad — cohabitation on the same shelf. We don't currently shard warmup across shelves reliably.
ajay: Quick probe: ran `ssh node-shelf03 'nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT'` and saw sustained high DMA/PCIe usage during the windows. Paste from node: ```
# timestamp  pcie_bytes_rx pcie_bytes_tx
00:01:12    980MB         1.1GB
00:01:13    1.0GB         1.2GB
```
maria: Oof. That explains NVLink/peer-to-peer slowdowns. Any quick mitigation we can flip?
sam: Two options short-term: 1) throttle warmup parallelism for us-west1-warmup (lower concurrency) 2) temporarily mark shelf-03 as warmup-exclude so onboards are routed elsewhere. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
linh: I'd prefer #1 first. We can tolerate slower warmups rather than disrupting production. Also reduces potential cost spike from re-routing.
opsbot: action: set-config us-west1-warmup-scaler --parallelism=2 (initiated by @maria) — ETA 30s
ajay: running a canary probe after the config flip. Using `curl http://metrics.local/api/query?node=shelf-03&metric=pcie_tx` to watch the tail.
maria: config rolled. Will monitor for 5m.
(2 min pass)
ajay: early signs good — pcie_tx dropped ~45% and queue depth lowered. Noisy bursts reduced.
sam: Nice. We should still follow up with a permanent plan: consider warmup reservation slices, or dedicated warmup shelves for heavy tenants. Also think about tagging high-volume onboards and applying backoff.
linh: Agreed. I'll open a doc to propose: `warmup-reservation-v1` with rollout plan and cost estimate.
maria: For bookkeeping: created INC-2026-194 to track root cause and mitigation steps, and assigned to lin h for follow-up.
ajay: One more FYI — we'll need to add signal to allocator to avoid mixing prefill-heavy tenants with latency-sensitive production on the same shelf. Might be a scheduler change (costly) but worth listing.
maria: Spike window has cleared. Tail latency back to baseline. Thanks all :thumbsup:
opsbot: deploybot: config change applied successfully on 3 nodes in us-west1-warmup.
linh: I'll add a short postmortem + cost tradeoffs to the doc and ping growth/product about onboarding throttles.
sam: TL;DR: short-term throttle worked. Long-term: reservation or scheduler isolation + labeling high-volume onboards.
maria: Closing thread. Will follow up in the doc.
